fixture.name: jwst_nonparametric_fits (PR #2014 sampler page)
fixture.why: the only non-tsnorm, non-degenerate fixture in the harness
fixture.platform: Linux x86_64, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, x64, box shared with two other agents (load 20-40); wall times indicative, R-hat/ESS/EEVPD deterministic given the seed
fixture.code_version: main @ fe6bda468 merged in (includes #2090 dead-fit guards)

headline: On the healthy fixture MCLMC returns a converged posterior in 46 s against NUTS's 189 s COLD -- but 75% of the NUTS wall is XLA compilation, not sampling. Warm, the same two fits are 36.0 s and 46.8 s, a 1.3x gap, and seconds-per-effective-sample is a tie (0.29 vs 0.31). The user's 'minutes not seconds' is therefore mostly COMPILE on this fixture, and the compile asymmetry is the real structural result: NUTS spends 142.6 s compiling its ragged tree-doubling control flow where MCLMC spends 10.4 s on a fixed-length scan, a 14x difference that no amount of sampling changes.

cold_vs_warm.method: same process, same ForwardModel, same seed, fit called twice; the campaign builds a fresh model per row and so measures the cold number
cold_vs_warm.caveat: the 3.6x / 45-vs-163 figure first reported was a COLD comparison and overstates the sampling advantage; quote 1.3x for warm sampling and the 14x compile gap separately

three_seed_sweep.protocol: six-seeds protocol cut to 3 by instruction; one fit per subprocess, sequential, cold per row

mcmc_nuts.config: n_warmup=1000, n_samples=400 (the page's own committed call)

mcmc_mclmc.config: n_warmup=5000, n_samples=20000 (a draw is one integrator step, not a trajectory)
mcmc_mclmc.divergences_note: unadjusted sampler: no accept/reject step, so no divergence count exists; energy_var_per_dim (EEVPD) is reported in its place against a 5e-4 target

three_seed_sweep.verdict: MCLMC clears the R-hat bar on 2/3 control seeds against NUTS's 1/3, at roughly half the median cold wall. Neither sampler clears it on all three. Seed 5 is the shared failure: NUTS pays 231.5 gradients per draw there and MCLMC collapses to min ESS 4.1, so that seed is a hard posterior for both rather than a sampler defect.

gradients_per_draw.note: the load-independent half of the comparison, and the one that survives a shared box
gradients_per_draw.mcmc_mclmc: 2.0, always -- one isokinetic McLachlan step per draw, no branch
gradients_per_draw.interpretation: MCLMC does NOT win by needing fewer gradients: on seed 4 it spends 645 gradients per effective sample against NUTS's 402. It wins on constant-cost, branch-free steps, which is also what makes it 14x cheaper to compile and what the vmapped catalog path wants.

status: control complete at 3 seeds; nb05 and nb00 next; tier NOT promoted pending the EEVPD anomaly
